# test_source_voltage.py
*`src/pySEA/rayTEM/tests/test_source_voltage.py`*

Tests for the optional accelerating voltage on `Source` and the `relativistic_wavelength` utility it derives its wavelength from.

Unlike the golden-artifact tests in `test_elements_sections_microscopes.py`, these are self-contained and write no files, so they can run in any order. The pair of voltage-set/voltage-unset tests is the point: `voltage` is additive, and the unset default must leave the `E` column at 0 so the existing ray goldens stay valid.

---

## Module-level functions

### `test_relativistic_wavelength_known_values()` *(line 15)*
Pins the utility against textbook values (200 kV -> 2.508 pm, 300 kV -> 1.969 pm) and asserts wavelength falls as voltage rises. These catch a dropped relativistic correction, which a non-relativistic formula would miss by roughly 5% at 200 kV.

<!-- AI: add cross-links and non-obvious notes here -->

### `test_relativistic_wavelength_rejects_nonpositive()` *(line 21)*
Zero and negative voltages raise `ValueError` rather than returning a nan or a complex number from the square root.

<!-- AI: add cross-links and non-obvious notes here -->

### `test_source_voltage_seeds_wavelength_and_energy_column()` *(line 30)*
End-to-end: a `Source(voltage=200)` exposes `voltage`, derives `wavelength` in metres, and fills the `E` column of every ray from `rays()` with the beam energy in keV.

<!-- AI: add cross-links and non-obvious notes here -->

### `test_source_without_voltage_stays_geometric()` *(line 38)*
The regression guard for the additive default. With no voltage, `wavelength` is `None` and `E` stays 0, which is what keeps the committed `.npy` ray goldens valid.

<!-- AI: add cross-links and non-obvious notes here -->

### `test_source_voltage_survives_reinstantiation()` *(line 46)*
`voltage` round-trips through `seashells.safeReinstantiate`, the save/load path. It survives because it is a constructor parameter; the derived `wavelength` is not, so it is recomputed rather than restored.
